message.content:
Here’s a quick reference to the **federal public holidays** that create long weekends in Canada for the year 2023.  
(If you’re planning for a specific province, let me know—some holidays are provincial only.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed On | Long‑Weekend Impact |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday, Jan 1 | Monday, Jan 2 | **Long weekend** (Sat–Mon) |
| Good Friday | Friday, Apr 7 | — | No long weekend (only one day) |
| Victoria Day | Monday, May 22 | — | **Long weekend** (Fri–Mon) |
| Canada Day | Saturday, Jul 1 | Monday, Jul 3 | **Long weekend** (Sat–Mon) |
| Labour Day | Monday, Sep 4 | — | **Long weekend** (Fri–Mon) |
| Thanksgiving | Monday, Oct 9 | — | **Long weekend** (Fri–Mon) |
| Christmas Day | Monday, Dec 25 | — | **Long weekend** (Fri–Mon) |

### Notes
- **New Year’s Day** is observed on the following Monday because the actual holiday falls on a Sunday.  
- **Canada Day** is also observed on Monday, Jul 3, since the actual holiday falls on a Saturday.  
- **Good Friday** is a federal holiday but does not create a long weekend because it is only one day.  
- **Remembrance Day** (Nov 11) is observed on Nov 10 (Friday) in 2023, so it does not create a long weekend.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like provincial holidays or more detailed information!
